_readme: Featured case studies. Only fields that have a value are shown on the site. Keys: problem, role, built, impact[] (list), stack[], link {label, href, note}. Fields with a null value are hidden; see _todo for what the owner still needs to supply. Facts come from the resume/LinkedIn/blog only. 'highlights' = big-number callouts, taken only from numbers already on the resume; when present they replace the Impact list.

items.title: The Weather Channel
items.problem: Serve 100M+ users with hurricane tracking, radar and live weather updates.
items.role: Senior Android Engineer, working with product, design and backend. Code reviews, architecture decisions and mentoring.
items.built: Server-driven UI (SDUI) screens, Adobe and analytics SDK integrations for personalization and safety tools, advanced concurrency, and test-driven development.
impact: Performance improved by 40% through advanced concurrency
items._todo: Owner: which metric is the 40% (cold start, jank, ANRs)? Confirm with the employer what may be published about internal work.

items.title: La3eb
items.problem: A social gaming and e-commerce platform with 1M+ active users.
items.role: Android Lead, and Senior Android Engineer before that. Led a team of 8 developers.
items.built: A modularized clean architecture, Jenkins CI/CD pipelines, mParticle and Braze integrations for engagement, and GraphQL.
impact: Development efficiency up 35% with new tools
items._todo: Owner: any concrete numbers for build time or release frequency?

items.title: KLLIQ
items.problem: A social app with large video and image uploads on a home timeline, realtime chat and push notifications.
items.built: A home timeline for large video and image uploads, realtime chat over Socket.IO, FCM push notifications and a custom ExoPlayer.
items._todo: Owner: any concrete result (upload reliability, chat latency)? Impact is hidden until supplied.

items.title: Android TV
items.built: An Android TV app with a custom ExoPlayer, built with Kotlin, Coroutines, Dagger Hilt, Paging 3, Room and the Leanback framework.
